answer.recommendation: Use fund fees as a screen: avoid funds in the most expensive third for equity and multi-asset menus, and do not select funds on last year's excess return alone, since past winners have not reliably repeated.

findings.text: In equity funds, each extra percentage point of annual expense ratio is associated with about 0.74 points less excess return the next year, and this is statistically significant.

Equity funds in the cheapest third returned about -5.0 points a year versus the CDI next year, against about -7.2 points in the most expensive third; all equity groups lagged the CDI, but the cheap group lagged least.
Over 10 years, a random equity fund ends at a median of 0.69 times the CDI wealth and beats the CDI 27% of the time; picking the cheapest third raises this only slightly to 0.72 and 30%.

Past performance is a weak guide. Among equity funds, last year's best quintile went on to return -2.23 points versus the CDI next year, close to the worst quintile's -3.34; the best-minus-worst gap of 1.11 is far inside its error range.

Persistence is somewhat better in fixed income, where the best group this year is more likely to stay best (39.3%, against a 20% chance), but even there the best-minus-worst next-year gap is only 0.14 points with a large error, and fixed income funds rarely beat the CDI over 10 years (14% for a random fund).

Fees do not explain multi-asset returns much (R-squared 0.019), and expense ratio slopes are negative but smaller than in equity; cheapest-third multi-asset funds returned -1.72 points versus -2.59 for the most expensive third.

risks: Results are associations over 2021-2025 and not causal effects; fees may correlate with other fund traits such as strategy or size that drive returns.
Four year pairs is a short history, so the persistence and fee estimates could change materially with more years or a different market regime.
Monte Carlo results assume returns are drawn independently from the sample and ignore fund closures and manager changes, which are only partly captured.
Most fund groups lagged the CDI on average over this period, so conclusions about relative ranking may not transfer to a different rate environment.
next_steps: Set a fee cap for equity and multi-asset menu options, targeting funds outside the most expensive third, and document the rule.
Stop using last year's excess return as the main selection criterion; review funds on fees, strategy fit and longer track records instead.
Re-run this analysis with additional years of data before revisiting any performance-based selection rule.
